Dialogue

/DY-uh-log/ — rhymes with analog · noun

Hear It

What It Means

A dialogue is a conversation between two or more people, especially one written into a play, book, or movie.

The movie's best dialogue is the rooftop argument between the two sisters.

Worked Example

In the play, the characters' witty dialogue about love and war reveals their intelligence and playfulness.

Dialogue is precise because it means conversation, especially in a written work—not just any communication, but back-and-forth speech. It captures the give-and-take between characters in a way that 'conversation' alone doesn't emphasize the literary/performed aspect.

How Dialogue Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

conversation

conversation: informal talk between people in daily life

monologue

monologue: a long speech given by one person

exchange

exchange: a back-and-forth trading of words or ideas

Antonyms

silence

silence: the complete absence of talk

soliloquy

soliloquy: a speech made alone, with no exchange

How Strong Is It? — monologue → conversation → dialogue → debate

monologue vs. dialogue

monologue vs. dialogue: A monologue sits below dialogue on the scale of exchange: in a monologue one voice speaks alone, while dialogue requires words to pass back and forth between speakers.

conversation vs. dialogue

conversation vs. dialogue: A conversation is looser than dialogue: conversation is everyday casual talk, while dialogue usually names the crafted, purposeful exchange written into a play or novel.

debate vs. dialogue

debate vs. dialogue: A debate is more intense than dialogue: dialogue is an open exchange of ideas, while a debate sharpens that exchange into a structured contest with sides to win.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — dia-

Prefix — dia-: across, between (Greek)

Root — logue

Root — logue: to speak; word, speech (Greek legein, logos)

Put it together

Put it together: Dia- ('across, between') + -logue ('to speak,' from Greek legein, logos) builds speech that passes between people - exactly what a dialogue is: a conversation exchanged between two or more speakers, especially one written into a play, book, or movie.

Use the root in a new word: monologue

Use the root in a new word: monologue: Before the play begins, one actor delivers a monologue alone on stage — mono- means 'one,' but the -logue root ('speech') is the very same one inside dialogue.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / literary

Dialogue is the word for written or performed conversation, especially when it's important to the story. For casual chat, 'conversation' works fine. When you want to emphasize the back-and-forth and the literary context, reach for dialogue.
